# Snowball English stemmer, ported to Rust

`rust/crates/gbrain-store/src/keyword/stem.rs` ports the English stemmer of PostgreSQL's `english_stem` text
search dictionary. That stemmer is code that the Snowball compiler generated, plus the Snowball runtime library.
Snowball is licensed under the BSD 3-clause licence. The complete licence text is `LICENSE` in this directory.
It is the `COPYING` file of the Snowball repository (`https://github.com/snowballstem/snowball`) at tag `v2.2.0`,
and it is byte for byte the same as `COPYING` at commit `d19326ac6c1b9a417fc872f7c2f845265a5e9ece`.

## What was ported

The port follows the files that PostgreSQL 18.6 ships in `src/backend/snowball/libstemmer/` and
`src/include/snowball/libstemmer/`:

- `stem_UTF_8_english.c`, the stemmer. Its header says "Generated by Snowball 2.2.0". `stem.rs` is a line by
  line port of it, and its `among` tables are the same data.
- the runtime, `utilities.c` and `api.c`: `get_utf8`, `skip_utf8`, the `*_grouping_U` functions, `find_among`
  and `find_among_b`.

PostgreSQL 18.6's `src/backend/snowball/README` says that directory is synced with Snowball git commit
`d19326ac6c1b9a417fc872f7c2f845265a5e9ece` of 2025-02-19. The version stamp inside the generated stemmer says
2.2.0. Both are recorded here because they are two different facts about the same files. The licence text is the
same at both.

The PostgreSQL parts of `stem.rs` (`dict_snowball.c` and `english.stop`) are described in
`third-party/postgresql/NOTICE.md`. `stem.rs` carries a one-line header that points to both notices.

## The word list in the English stemming golden

`rust/crates/gbrain-store/tests/fixtures/english_stem.tsv` has two columns: a word, and what PostgreSQL 18.6
returns for `ts_lexize('english_stem', word)`. The lexeme column always comes from PostgreSQL, never from
Snowball directly. The 50,477 words are, in order:

1. Rows 1 to 42,649: the sample vocabulary `english/voc.txt` of the Snowball data repository
   (`https://github.com/snowballstem/snowball-data`), at commit `ca1919d397e11f83ea08de2dbb4126679f592ca5`,
   byte for byte and in file order. That repository has its own licence file, `COPYING`, with the same BSD
   3-clause terms. Its text at that commit is `LICENSE-snowball-data` in this directory. The `english`
   directory there has no licence file of its own.
2. 7,828 more words written for this test: the English stopwords in upper and title case, about 5,800 sampled
   vocabulary words in upper, title and mixed case, an empty string, a space, hand-written edge cases (apostrophes,
   non-ASCII case folding, CJK, emoji, digits, suffix fragments, a 70-character word), and 1,843 random
   combinations of English suffix fragments with letters and apostrophes. The random seed was not kept, so these
   words exist only in the committed file.

How to check the lexeme column against PostgreSQL 18.6 is in `third-party/postgresql/NOTICE.md` (the
`regen-search-goldens.ts` command).
